minutes.headline: Select Board and School Committee agreed to skip a FY26 override and use free cash; a larger override is planned for next year.
minutes.summary: A joint session with the School Committee centered on whether to put an override on the May ballot. The town manager and most school members favored no override this year, a one-time free cash bridge, and a joint override next year; the Select Board members voiced their positions with no formal vote. In the regular meeting the board heard DPW trash route changes, zoning articles, the Marshall Park borrowing plan and the FY26 budget and warrant walk-through, opted out of in-person early voting, waived the right of first refusal on 100 Townsend Harbor Road, approved minutes and went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: Supported the fire fourth-shift focus and ambulance enterprise fund idea, opposed changing the health insurance premium split, and said the vote on the right of first refusal for 100 Townsend Harbor Road was premature given the 120-day window.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager's proposed budget reduced the pavement management line to zero to help balance the budget.
Superintendent said bridging the school gap would need about two million dollars, not including a one-time transfer.

budget_items.topic: Restoring town-side items with an override
budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager said an override this year would also need to restore pavement management and debt service savings used to balance the budget.
Town manager presented free cash and said it is slightly under the recommended percentage of the budget.
Policy sends a share to OPEB and stabilization funds; the pre-meeting plan totaled a stated amount.
Snow and ice deficiency, special education move-in, a grant clean-up and FY26 capital are funded from free cash, leaving starting free cash for next year.
Town manager could forgo stabilization deposits and use some starting free cash to give about half a million to schools.
Town manager gave the balance and said no spending plan for the fund has been seen.
Town manager presented total revenues, mostly property tax, with new growth estimated conservatively.
State aid is based on the Governor's budget (House 1) with assessments and sweeps netted out.
Motor vehicle excise is a large share of local receipts and may need revisiting before town meeting; investment income has been far above projection.
Town manager walked through the new revenue and its split between town, schools and Monty Tech.
General stabilization is above the 5% target; OPEB transfer of 10% of free cash is the policy; OPEB is lightly funded against a large liability.
Special projects article covers decommissioning, assessor directives and road repair; snow and ice deficit projected; CARES grant clearing.
Debt roll-off lowers debt service; part supports the capital plan and the remainder balances the operating budget, which is not best practice.
Health insurance rises sharply but the line was budgeted closer to actual; Medicare, salary reserve and unemployment (if layoffs occur) noted.
The budget holds funds for grant help that went unused; town manager suggested a grant and contract manager; board split on grant writer versus manager.
The network administrator position will not be filled and its money will go to the IT contractor, with an aim to reduce on-site days.

budget_items.topic: Police K9 and comfort dog handler pay
budget_items.what_was_said: Handlers must be compensated; the police budget carries a large percentage increase for K9 care.
Fire budget rises slightly on EMS supplies and excludes the fourth shift, which would be close to half a million.
Hudson joining saves the town a small amount; dispatch assessment stays about level.

budget_items.topic: DPW pavement management and snow and ice
budget_items.what_was_said: Pavement management was requested higher, reduced to zero, and snow and ice raised to narrow the usual deficit.
Spreadsheet showed plan scenarios under different Chapter 90 amounts; Chapter 90 increase may offset part of the cut.
Town manager named trash and recycling and mosquito control as places to cut if pavement management is restored in the levy.

budget_items.topic: Free cash arithmetic for pavement plan
budget_items.what_was_said: Member ran numbers on starting free cash versus finding money for the pavement plan.
Member noted the school line shows an increase percentage different from the expected one; manager to check the formula.
County retirement rises and the health insurance increase is expected to persist, driven by GLP-1 drugs; employee/employer premium split debated.
An unfunded placeholder article for the track and field drainage work was not ranked highly by the capital committee.
Parks Commission proposed a debt-excluded borrowing for the full project, with a reduced phase-one fallback.
Prior state grants were released when scope shrank; commission plans to reapply with professional grant writing help.
Capital funds were appropriated for townwide keying and security and a state-list vendor is being contracted.

budget_items.topic: Right of first refusal purchase price
budget_items.what_was_said: Purchase price of the parcel exceeds what the town could fund.

decisions.decision: Select Board members indicated, without a vote, that they would follow the guidance of no override this year and use one-time funds, with a comprehensive override next year.
Board chose not to move the date of town meeting and to add extra single-topic meetings instead.
An additional meeting was set for the 19th to continue budget and warrant discussion.
Town manager will rework the grant manager proposal (grant and contract manager) after board feedback.
Town manager will speak with the DPW director about using Chapter 90 for the DPW vehicle items.
Board held off reviewing the list of upcoming board and committee vacancies.

what_happened.line: In a joint session, Select Board members indicated without a vote that they would follow guidance of no FY26 override, a one-time free cash bridge, and a larger override next year.
The board voted unanimously to opt out of in-person early voting for the local annual town election.
The board voted 4-0-1 to waive the town's right of first refusal on 100 Townsend Harbor Road.
The town manager said free cash could fund year-end transfers and warrant items, and that some starting free cash could give schools a one-time bridge.
The board chose to add single-topic meetings rather than move town meeting, and set an extra meeting for the 19th on the budget and warrant.

why_it_matters: Using one-time free cash for the schools' FY26 gap means no override question on the May ballot this year, but it does not fix the underlying gap, so residents may be asked to vote on a larger override next year.
The FY26 budget as presented balanced partly by reducing pavement management to zero, so road maintenance funding is one of the items an override or later decision would need to restore.
